newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan sends trade convoy to Central Asia.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan sends trade convoy to Central Asia.

text.p: Pakistan, eager to build trade ties with oil-rich Central Asian states, sent a 20-truck convoy to China on Thursday on its way to the Kazakh capital Almaty, the official APP news agency said.
The trucks carrying rice, wheat and leather goods left the city of Rawalpindi near Islamabad on November 5 and reached Gilgit town on Wednesday, it said. They left for China on Thursday.
The convoy was expected to return to Karachi after 27 days, accompanied by 60 more trucks, 20 each from China, Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan.

The convoy's torturous trip, trundling up the mountainous Karakoram Highway and across the Khunjerab Pass to the Chinese market town of Kashgar and on to the Kyrgyz capital Bishkek before winding up in Almaty, was expected to take nine days.
Strife in Afghanistan, across which the most direct access routes run, has long foiled Pakistan's ambitions to promote Karachi as a port serving landlocked Central Asian countries.
Pakistan sent a convoy through Afghanistan in October 1994 to open a trade route with Turkmenistan, but Afghan guerrilla commanders seized the trucks in the southern city of Kandahar.
The radical Islamic Taleban, then virtually unknown, rescued the convoy, routed the local commanders and captured Kandahar, now their headquarters. The convoy finally got through.

Pakistan, China, Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan agreed in 1994 to encourage trade by improving the 1,284-km (798-mile) Karakoram highway, completed by Chinese engineers and Pakistani troops in 1978. The trade convoy to Almaty has been planned since June.
The four countries also agreed to keep the levy transport charges to the level their own nationals would pay.
